user.title: Connect to Dockhand
user.description: Enter your Dockhand server URL. An API token will be requested if authentication is enabled.

data_description.api_url: The base URL of your Dockhand instance.
data_description.verify_ssl: Uncheck to allow self-signed or untrusted SSL certificates. Only disable if your Dockhand instance uses a self-signed cert.

token.title: Dockhand API Token
token.description: Your Dockhand server requires authentication. Generate an API token in Dockhand under **Profile → API tokens**, then paste it here.

data_description.api_token: A Dockhand API token starting with dh_. Generate one under Profile → API tokens in the Dockhand UI.

setup_options.title: Configure polling and features
setup_options.description: Set how often to poll Dockhand and which optional entity groups to enable. All of these can be changed later via Configure.

data.poll_interval: Fast poll interval (seconds) — stats, containers & stacks
data.poll_interval_slow: Slow poll interval (seconds) — images, volumes, networks, schedules

data_description.poll_interval: How often to refresh container, stack, and environment stats. Default: 60. Minimum: 10.
data_description.poll_interval_slow: How often to refresh images, volumes, networks, and schedules. Default: 600. Minimum: 30.
data_description.enable_schedules: Enables sensors for Dockhand maintenance schedules.
data_description.enable_images: Enables sensors for Docker images on each environment.
data_description.enable_volumes: Enables sensors for Docker volumes on each environment.
data_description.enable_networks: Enables sensors for Docker networks on each environment.
data_description.enable_runtime_controls: Creates number/select entities to change a stack-less container's CPU, memory, and process limits, and restart policy, live. Not available for Compose-managed containers.
data_description.enable_container_stats: Creates per-container CPU, memory, network, and disk I/O sensors. Off by default since it's a lot of entities most people don't need; turning it off also removes any already-created ones.
data_description.enable_update_entities: Creates a Home Assistant update entity for every container. Turn this off if you manage updates another way and don't want Dockhand's containers in HA's own update management. Also hides the 'Update all' button; 'Check for updates' keeps working either way.
data_description.enable_precise_updates: Upgrades update entities to show precise version numbers (image digests) via periodic registry queries, instead of just an image tag. Requires 'Enable update entities' above.
data_description.poll_interval_updates: How often to run the registry queries above (seconds). Default: 86400 (24 hours). Minimum: 300.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Dockhand
reauth_confirm.description: Your API token is no longer valid. Generate a new token in Dockhand under **Profile → API tokens** and enter it below.

data_description.api_token: A Dockhand API token starting with dh_.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Dockhand
reconfigure.description: Update the server URL, SSL setting, or API token. To change polling intervals or feature flags, use Configure instead.

data_description.api_url: The base URL of your Dockhand instance.
data_description.verify_ssl: Uncheck to allow self-signed or untrusted SSL certificates.
data_description.api_token: Your current token is shown masked. Clear it and save to disable authentication (you will be prompted again if the server still requires it). Enter a new value to rotate credentials.

error.cannot_connect: Unable to connect to Dockhand. Check the API URL and network connectivity.
error.invalid_auth: Invalid API token. Make sure you copied the full token starting with dh_.

abort.already_configured: This Dockhand instance is already configured.

runtime_update_warning.title: Dockhand reported a warning updating {container}
runtime_update_warning.description:
Changing {field} on container "{container}" succeeded, but Dockhand's underlying Docker Engine call returned a warning, which may mean it wasn't fully applied: {warnings}

Check the container in the Dockhand UI to confirm the current value.

runtime_memory_reverted.title: Memory limit auto-reverted for {container}
runtime_memory_reverted.description: Container "{container}" stopped running shortly after its memory limit was lowered, which can happen when the new limit is below the container's actual usage and the kernel enforces it immediately. The memory limit has been automatically reverted to its previous value ({memory_bytes} bytes). Check the container's logs and current health in Dockhand.
